protocol.description:
The purpose of this protocol is to provide a way for Linux based compositors to identify the process a toplevel belongs to.
This protocol depends on the ext-foreign-toplevel-list protocol.
The compositor may choose to restrict this protocol to a special client launched by the compositor itself or expose it to all clients, this is compositor policy.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backwards incompatible major versions of the protocol are to be expected. Exposing this protocol without an opt-in mechanism is discouraged.

interface.name: phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_manager_v1
interface.description: The global object used to initialize the extension interfaces to get the pidfd of a toplevel.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_manager_v1 object anymore.
Any objects already created through this instance are not affected.

request.name: get_pidfd

description.summary: create the object to send the pidfd

request.description:
This request creates an extension object to receive the pidfd for the foreign toplevel.
It is illegal to destroy the ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 before the phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1 object is destroyed and must result in a orphaned error.

interface.name: phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1
interface.description:
This object receives the toplevels pidfd. It extends the ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 interface.
If a compositor implementation sends the xx_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1.finished event, the compositor must not send any more phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1.pidfd events.
A pidfd references the toplevel's process identifier (pid) via a file descriptor see pidfd_open(1).

event.name: pidfd
event.description: This event is emitted for a toplevel window once its pidfds is known to the compositor. If the pidfd can't be determined, no event is sent.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor has finished with the pidfd manager

event.description: This event indicates that the compositor is done sending events to this object. The client should destroy the object. See phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1.destroy for more information.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1 object anymore.

enum.name: error
enum.description: These errors are sent in response to phoc_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1 requests.

entry.name: orphaned
entry.summary: the ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 object was destroyed before the xx_foreign_toplevel_pidfd_v1
